chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Keep on guard against the slipping away of blessings because not everything that runs away comes back.

key_terms.شَارِدٍ: One that scatters, runs away, or wanders off
key_terms.نِفَارَ: Slipping away, escaping, or scattering (from blessings)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to guard against the slipping away of blessings in Shia teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against the subtle negligence (nifār) that leads to the loss of divine blessings, emphasizing that not every scattered opportunity or favor returns. This teaching, found in Nahj al-Balagha, reflects the Shia understanding of *ni'mah* as a dynamic trust requiring active gratitude and vigilance rather than passive receipt. The metaphor underscores the fragility of spiritual and material favors, urging believers to maintain constant awareness to prevent their irreversible loss.
